result.summary:
Independently re-gated docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-030.md (branch feature/WF02-REQ-030, commit 34a8085) against WF-02 Step 3b's three checks, re-deriving every load-bearing claim from the real code rather than trusting TEST-DESIGNER's result.summary.

Read docs/agents/instructions/core-directives.md, WF-02 Step 3b, docs/agents/design/REQ-030.md in full (all 6 ACs plus the open questions), and docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-030.md in full.

1) AC4's phone-normalization claim, re-derived independently: `apps/bot/src/domain/walkin.ts` line 80-82, `normalizePhoneForMatching(phone) { return phone.replace(/[^0-9]/g, ""); }` -- a pure digit-strip exactly matching design §3.2's stated rule. Traced both fixture strings against this exact regex by hand: `"+77074445566"` -> strip `+` -> `"77074445566"` (11 digits); `"7 707 444-55-66"` -> strip the three spaces and the two dashes -> `"77074445566"` (same 11 digits, same order). The two literally collide under this implementation, not merely under the spec's assertion of what the regex should do. TEST-DESIGNER's claim to have run this verification is corroborated -- the claimed result matches direct re-derivation exactly.

2) Cross-context forgery case's authorization re-derivation claim, re-derived independently against `apps/bot/src/handlers/walkin.ts`: `makeWalkinConfirmCallbackHandler` (lines 162-200) extracts `eventId` exclusively from `WALKIN_CONFIRM_PATTERN.exec(ctx.callbackQuery?.data ?? "")` (line 164) -- the callback_data string. `parseWalkinMessageFields` (called at line 192, defined at domain/walkin.ts lines 191-211) is invoked only AFTER eventId is already resolved and only to recover `name`/`company`/`phone` from the message text; its return shape (`{ name, company, phone }`) carries no `eventId` field at all, confirmed by reading the function body -- it slices only `Name:`/`Company:`/`Phone:` lines, never an `Event:`-derived id (matching design §7.1's explicit statement that the Event: line is never parsed back into a used value). Re-authorization: line 171-176 resolves `tgId = ctx.from?.id` (the TAPPER's own Telegram id, not anything from the message) and line 186 calls `requireOrganizerForChapter(db, BigInt(tgId), event.chapterId)` fresh, on every invocation of this handler, using `event.chapterId` freshly read via `getEventById(db, eventId)` (line 179) keyed off the callback_data-derived eventId -- never a cached/passed-through value from an earlier call. The override handler (lines 205-242) repeats the identical sequence verbatim. Both of TEST-DESIGNER's and this run's task brief's claims are independently confirmed: eventId is callback_data-only, and authorization re-derives fresh from the tapping identity every time.

3) AC6's EventStaff-vs-plain-member distinction, verified meaningful: `apps/bot/src/domain/eventAuthorization.ts`'s `checkOrganizerForChapter` (lines 60-78) branches purely on `user.role` ("member" -> refused; "owner" -> allowed; "organizer" -> allowed only if `user.chapterId === targetChapterId`) -- it reads a role column on the user, and never queries or joins `event_staff` anywhere in its body or in `requireOrganizerForChapter`'s (lines 81-88) one-line delegation to it. A user holding a genuine `event_staff` row for the exact event but role `"member"` is refused at the `user.role === "member"` branch regardless of that row's existence -- confirming AC6's fixture (a real EventStaff row for this exact event, not merely absent staff) is a strictly stronger test than a plain-member fixture: it is the only fixture shape capable of catching a hypothetical future regression that widens this check with an `event_staff`-membership OR-branch, since a plain-member fixture with no staff row anywhere would pass under both correct and regressed code.

4) Malformed-message case's two sub-variants, checked for genuine distinctness: `parseWalkinMessageFields` (domain/walkin.ts lines 191-211) tests `nameLine === undefined || companyLine === undefined || phoneLine === undefined` as a single compound condition -- both the missing-Phone and missing-Name sub-cases trigger the SAME line of code (the same `if`), not two structurally distinct code paths. The spec does not overclaim otherwise: it frames the second sub-variant explicitly as "a second, cheap assertion, not a second seeded fixture" confirming the OR-condition's `undefined`-detection works for more than one of the three operands, rather than claiming two distinct branches. This is an honest, correctly-scoped framing, not a coverage-inflation defect -- no rework needed.

5) Cross-checked exact expected values against the real implementation: `formatWalkinConfirmMessage`'s four-line canonical format, `COMPANY_PLACEHOLDER`'s round-trip in `parseWalkinMessageFields`, `requireOrganizerForChapter`'s three-argument signature (db, tgId, chapterId), and `commitWalkin`'s outcome/audit-action table all match the design doc's §5/§6/§7 tables and the spec's stated assertions verbatim -- no drift found between design, spec, and code.

6) No mocked/stubbed grammY Context: grepped the spec for mock/jest.fn/vi.fn/stub/'as unknown as Context' -- zero matches. Every case (AC1, AC3 override-confirm/dismiss, AC4, AC5 dynamic, AC6, cross-context forgery, malformed-message) dispatches through real `bot.handleUpdate()` via the shared `makeTestBot()`/`commandUpdate`/`callbackUpdate` helpers modeled on BACKEND-DEV's already-committed `walkin.db.test.ts` pattern (confirmed that file's own `makeTestBot`/`new Bot(...)`/`bot.handleUpdate` usage directly). AC5's static check is explicitly and correctly framed as a source-level git grep, not a vitest case pretending to be a dispatch.

7) Every case states its own specific failure mode (AC1: a userId-resolution bug overwriting the organizer's own profile in place without changing row counts; AC3 override: collapsing the two-step override or mislabeling previousAdmission; AC3 dismiss: walkin:cancel accidentally wired to commitWalkin; AC4: a normalizePhoneForMatching/getUserIdByPhone regression creating a duplicate User/Profile; AC5: a query widened to include phone, or a future log.info call added to the flow; AC6: an ||-widened authorization check accepting EventStaff membership; cross-context forgery: authorization derived from message content/button existence rather than the tapper's own identity; malformed-message: an unhandled exception or a silent empty-string default proceeding into commitWalkin) -- none reduce to 'check it looks right.'

8) File-existence claim verified, not trusted: `git log --all --oneline -- apps/bot/src/handlers/walkin.forgery.test.ts` returns nothing -- the spec's repeated statement that this file does not exist yet (TEST-RUNNER writes it at Step 4) is accurate, matching the REQ-026/027/028/029 precedent.

9) tg_id range check: `walkin.db.test.ts` (BACKEND-DEV's committed file) declares `nextTgId = 942_000_000` (confirmed by direct grep) -- this spec's stated 943_000_000+ range for the new file is genuinely distinct from it and from every other range the spec enumerates. The tg_id collision the spec flags is between `checkinQr.forgery.test.ts` (REQ-029's not-yet-written spec) and `walkin.db.test.ts` (already committed) -- unrelated to this spec's own 943M range, correctly identified as ISS-0026 already filed separately, not a defect in this spec.

Gate checks: (a) every acceptance criterion has >=1 verification case -- AC1/AC3/AC4/AC5/AC6 each have a dedicated new case; AC2 is correctly deferred to BACKEND-DEV's already-committed walkin.db.test.ts with a stated no-gap finding matching REQ-029's own precedent -- PASS. (b) no TODO left -- `grep -in TODO docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-030.md` returns zero matches -- PASS. (c) each case is precise enough to run without judgment -- every case names the exact fixture (specific names/phones/company values/capacity), exact dispatch sequence (real command/callback payloads, exact message-text corruption), and exact pass/fail assertions (exact catalog keys, exact SQL predicates/row-count deltas, exact audit action strings) -- PASS.

No issues found requiring rework.

checks.every_ac_has_a_case: PASS -- AC1/AC3/AC4/AC5/AC6 each have a dedicated new case in walkin.forgery.test.ts (design); AC2 correctly deferred to BACKEND-DEV's committed walkin.db.test.ts with a stated no-gap finding on direct read; cross-context forgery and malformed-message are correctly additional coverage beyond the six ACs, per this run's task brief.
checks.no_todo_left: PASS -- grep -in TODO on docs/agents/test-specs/REQ-030.md: zero matches.
checks.cases_precise_and_runnable: PASS -- every case names the exact fixture, exact dispatch/callback sequence including exact message-text corruption, and exact pass/fail assertions (catalog keys, SQL predicates, row-count deltas, audit action strings) -- none rely on a subjective 'looks right' judgment.
checks.ac4_normalization_claim_verified: PASS -- direct read of normalizePhoneForMatching (domain/walkin.ts lines 80-82, phone.replace(/[^0-9]/g, "")) and hand-traced both fixture strings ('+77074445566' and '7 707 444-55-66') against it confirm both strip to the identical digit string '77074445566'. TEST-DESIGNER's claimed verification is corroborated exactly.
checks.cross_context_forgery_reauth_claim_verif: PASS -- direct read of handlers/walkin.ts confirms eventId is extracted only from WALKIN_CONFIRM_PATTERN.exec(ctx.callbackQuery?.data) (never from parseWalkinMessageFields's output, which carries no eventId field), and requireOrganizerForChapter is called fresh on every invocation using the TAPPER's own ctx.from.id and a freshly re-read event.chapterId -- confirmed identically in both the confirm and override handlers.
checks.ac6_eventstaff_distinction_verified: PASS -- checkOrganizerForChapter (eventAuthorization.ts lines 60-78) branches purely on user.role and never queries event_staff at all, confirming a genuine EventStaff-row fixture is a strictly stronger negative test than a plain-member fixture -- it is the only fixture shape that could catch a future ||-widened check.
checks.malformed_message_subvariants_checked: PASS with honest framing -- both sub-variants (missing Phone:, missing Name:) trigger the same compound-OR condition in parseWalkinMessageFields, not two distinct code branches; the spec correctly frames the second as 'a cheap additional assertion' rather than overclaiming distinct code paths -- not a defect.
checks.no_mocked_context: PASS -- zero mock/jest.fn/vi.fn/stub hits in the spec; every case dispatches through real bot.handleUpdate() via makeTestBot(), modeled on BACKEND-DEV's own committed walkin.db.test.ts pattern (confirmed directly).
checks.failure_modes_stated: PASS -- every case states a specific, mechanism-level failure mode.
checks.file_existence_claim_verified: PASS -- git log --all --oneline -- apps/bot/src/handlers/walkin.forgery.test.ts returns nothing, confirming the spec's claim that this file does not yet exist.
checks.tgid_range_verified: PASS -- walkin.db.test.ts's actual nextTgId (942_000_000, grep-confirmed) is distinct from this spec's stated 943_000_000+ range; the flagged ISS-0026 collision (checkinQr.forgery.test.ts vs walkin.db.test.ts, both 942M) is correctly attributed elsewhere and already filed.
